title: The servants of the Merciful
tomorrow: what does a wise father say about his son's voice?

lines: A SHARP REPLY, EASY TO LOAD.
cards: Someone snaps at you over a coffee order, or leaves a sharp comment under your post, or cuts in front of you in the pickup line. A sharp reply is easy to load, and quick to send.
Surah al-Furqan has its own answer, the first stroke of a portrait.
In Pickthall's words: "The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace."

teach.b: The question is old: how do you answer someone who's rude? The Qur'an answers with a portrait, not a rule. The servants of the Merciful spend nights before their Lord, bowing and standing.
When they spend, they are "neither prodigal nor grudging; and there is ever a firm station between the two." They don't bear false witness, and when they pass by idle talk, they pass with dignity.

They pray for their spouses and children to be a comfort to their eyes. And for anyone who's failed at all of it, there's a door: for those who turn back and do good, "Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds."
Walking gently is just the first brushstroke. Now a neighbor.

The book of Proverbs, read by Jews and Christians, says it in the King James words: "A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger." The same instinct: meet heat with gentleness, not more heat.
And one honest difference. Proverbs speaks as practical wisdom and names what a soft answer does: it turns away wrath. Al-Furqan describes who the servants are.
They answer Peace, and the verse never promises the other person will calm down.
One points to a result, the other to a character.
Same gentleness, two reasons for it, and neither cancels the other.

how: The closing verses of al-Furqan are read as a picture of good character, and the word salam, peace, is the everyday Muslim greeting.

games.q: what does “the servants of the merciful” mean?
o: the angels who carry the Throne of God
the people al-Furqan portrays as belonging to God
the companions who moved with the Prophet to Madina

games.q: the portrait, stroke by stroke — tap the pairs.
p: a soft answer turneth away wrath

s: the servants of the Merciful answer rudeness with peace
when the foolish address them, they answer: Peace (25:63).
the passage promises the rude person will calm down
it describes who the servants are; it promises nothing about the other person.
the portrait is only about being gentle in speech
it covers nights of prayer, spending, honesty, family, and turning back after wrong.

games.q: Jordan's grandma hears Amira quote 'they answer: Peace' and says her Bible says a soft answer turns away wrath. Jordan asks: same thing?
o: close kin: both meet heat gently; Proverbs names what it does, the Qur'an who they are.
the same: every scripture says the same thing in different words.
opposites: one says be soft, the other says stand your ground.
games.why: shared ground and an honest difference: Proverbs points to a result (wrath turned away); al-Furqan to a character (they answer Peace, whatever comes back).

practice: Pick one trait from the portrait to walk with: modestly, with dignity, or answering peace. If you can, stand and walk slowly for a minute, across a room or down a hall, heel then toe, as if the floor could feel you.
Then sit for the rest of the time, and let your breathing walk just as gently.

wordCard.voice: The servants of the Merciful. 'Ibad ar-Rahman: people in al-Furqan known by how they walk, answer, spend and pray.

orig.note: Arabic: the servants of the Most Merciful (25:63).

carryVoice: The line to keep: walk gently, and answer Peace whether or not it lands. That's the day.
